\abstract{\textbf{Motivation:} Exact pairwise alignment guarantees an optimal alignment under the chosen costs, unaffected by the cut-offs of heuristic aligners, and is the ground truth against which those aligners are evaluated. No single exact algorithm, however, is fastest across workloads: diagonal transition excels on near-identical pairs, bit-parallel band doubling on long divergent reads, and inter-sequence vectorisation on batches of short pairs.\\
\textbf{Results:} We present dinara-align, an exact aligner that selects its algorithm for each pair without giving up optimality. Switches prompted by runtime estimates wait until the current search has spent a small fixed share of the alternative's least work, so estimates misled by clustered errors no longer abandon searches that would finish; a gap-affine alignment adds a second wavefront search only when measured work shows two would be cheaper, which we prove keeps it optimal; and short pairs are aligned in narrow bands that each vector lane certifies optimal. On one Intel Skylake-X core and 25 datasets from 250~bp reads to 1~Mbp pairs, dinara-align was the fastest exact aligner at unit costs, up to 2.4 times faster than A*PA2 on ultra-long nanopore reads and 1.9 and 5.1 times faster than WFA on Illumina and HiFi reads, and at gap-affine costs the fastest on every dataset any tool completed, tied with WFA on Illumina reads.\\
\textbf{Availability and implementation:} dinara-align is free software under the Mozilla Public License 2.0, available at \url{https://github.com/kokyriakidis/dinara-align} with C, C++, Python and command-line interfaces.}
